Cement factory in Manipur
2646. SHRI RISHANG KEISHING:
Will the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF
NORTH EASTERN REGION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that lime stone
deposits are available to start an
economically viable cement factory in
Manipur;
(b) if so, the quantity of the deposit and
also the quality of the lime stone;
(c) whether the State Government has
proposed a 200 M.T. Capacity per day
cement factory in the State; and
(d) if so, Government's response
thereto?
Development of NER
2647. SHRI DRUPAD BORGOHAIN:
Will the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF
NORTH EASTERN REGION be pleased
to state:
(a) the steps taken for the Development
of North Eastern Region after the formation
of the Ministry;
(b) whether projects have been
sanctioned for different States of the Region;
and
(c) if so, what are those?
PSUs for disinvestment
†2648. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have selected
those PSUs for disinvestment where
production has almost stopped but
Government expenditure is still being
incurred;
(b) if so, the names of those PSUs;
(c) the details of the assessment made
with regard to their movable and immovable
properties; and
(d) the amount collected as a result of
their disinvestment?

585
WIN2\SESSION\2751RS 585
Meeting of core group of Secretaries on
disinvestment of ITDC Hotels
2649. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the core group of Secretaries
on disinvestment met on 26th June, 2002 to
deliberate on the bids for six hotels of India
Tourism Development Corporation;
(b) if so, the main points discussed;
(c) the decisions arrived at; and
(d) the steps being taken to implement
them?
Disinvestment of blue-chip PSUs
2650. SHRI BALWANT SINGH
RAMOOWALIA: Will the Minister of
DISINVESTMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to divest between 10 to 25 per cent stake in
five leading blue-chip PSUs in order to raise
a whopping Rs. 28,500 crore as reported in
Hindustan Times dated 26th July, 2002;
(b) if so, the details of receipt from sale
of equity in the open market, company-
wise, dilution in percentage and proceeds in
crore;
(c) whether Government also propose
to mop up Rs. 24,800 crore through strategic
sales in eight other undertakings; and
(d) if so, the projected price realisation
thereof from strategic sale, IPOs, company-
wise?
Disinvestment of PSUs in Assam
2651. SHRI DRUPAD BORGOHAIN:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) the PSUs in Assam which
Government propose to disinvest during the
year 2002-2003;
(b) the fund expected to be raised by this
process; and
(c) the time-frame of completing
privatisation in PSUs in Assam?
Chinese vaccine for Japanese
Encephalitis
2652. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Chinese
vaccine-derived recombinant type Japanese
Encephalitis vaccine - is also more effective
for Japanese Encephalitis;
(b) if so, whether any consultation has
been done in this connection with the
Peoples' Republic of China;
(c) if not, whether Government propose
to do so keeping in view the prevalence of
Japanese Encephalitis in the country
particularly in Andhra Pradesh; and
(d) whether Government will involve
WHO/UNICEF in this evaluation
programme?
Telemedicine facility
2653. PROF. M. SANKARA-
LINGAM: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Prime Minister has
recently inaugurated a Telemedicine Project
in New Delhi and physicians at a Chennai
hospital advised two heart patients in Port
Blair;

(b) if so, the salient features of this
project; and
(c) how does his Ministry propose to
spread this facility to the nook and corner of
the country?
Non-functional CT-scan machines in
MCD-run hospitals
2654. SHRI MOOLCHAND MEENA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:

the past couple of years, CT-scan machines
installed in the Capital's two MCD-run
hospitals have been out of order;
(b) if so, whether the machines, costing
over Rs. 2.35 crores each were installed in
1993 but after they stopped functioning in
1999, they have neither been repaired nor
